description:
Integration test `chat_set_duplicate_direct_cleanup_destroy_failure_redacts_backend_display` in `crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs` (line ~1823) passes when run alone (`cargo test -p jmap-chat-server --test integration chat_set_duplicate_direct_cleanup_destroy_failure_redacts_backend_display`) but fails when the full test binary is run (`cargo test -p jmap-chat-server --all-features` or `--workspace`).

Confirmed reproducible on commit 86e185d (current HEAD) before any in-flight changes.

The failure shows the chat create unexpectedly succeeded:
- Test expects `notCreated[c0]` with type=serverFail
- Actual response has `created[c0]` with the full Chat object

This is a classic test-ordering / shared-state hazard. Either:
1. The test's chat-cleanup setup leaks state from a prior test that ran in the same binary, causing the duplicate-direct guard to misfire (or not fire).
2. The 'duplicate direct' detection depends on global state that a parallel test is mutating.

Surfaced during bd:JMAP-qz9v.48 (resolve_query_offset propagation), where the full workspace test run flagged this as a regression — but it pre-exists the change, so this is its own bead.

Investigation hints:
- Check whether the test seeds an Id::from("contact-1") and whether another test in the same binary races on that contact id.
- Compare with sister tests around line 1820-1885 — there are several chat-cleanup-failure tests; only this one is flaky.
- Possibly fix by giving the test a unique contact id per-run, or by spawning the MemoryBackend per-test.

Not caused by JMAP-qz9v.48 propagation; the bead is filed so the resolve_query_offset commit can land without absorbing the responsibility for fixing this pre-existing flake.
title: chat_set_duplicate_direct_cleanup_destroy_failure_redacts_backend_display fails in full suite, passes in isolation — test ordering / shared state
